findings.finding: Management's own Q2 colour builds to a revenue figure at or just below the $90.92M consensus, and management has beaten its own colour recently. The Q1 call gave subscription growth 'close to 30%' on Q2 FY26's ~$33.4M (=> ~$43.4M), professional services 'around current levels' (~$19.6M), products 'around $10 million per quarter', and maintenance ~$17.3-17.5M. That sums to ~$90.3M, 0.7% below consensus. But Q1 revenue was 'better than management expected', Q1 adj. EBITDA came in at 20.8% against ~16% flagged on 2026-06-03, and revenue beat consensus in Q2 FY26 ($79.3M vs $76.9M), Q3 FY26 ($80.4M vs $79M) and Q1 FY27 ($87.7M vs $86.0M). Net read: revenue roughly +0.5% to +1.5% versus the bar, inside the guided FY range.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The revenue line has not decided the reaction. In Jan 2026 a revenue beat ($80.4M vs $79M) fell -20% on an EPS miss and an implied Q4 subscription deceleration. In Oct 2025 a 3% beat with a raised guide rose +22.6%. In Jul 2026 a 2% beat with a raised guide rose +7.2% (baseline history; https://www.itiger.com/news/1107151489).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced. Consensus already sits at the arithmetic of the colour, and if the Street expected a big beat the range would sit above $91.7M. What is not in the number is the conservatism habit: a Street that priced it would carry a consensus a point or two above the colour build, not on it.
findings.independence: Q2 FY26 split (recurring $51.0M, 65.5% subscription) from the Oct-2025 release via https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20251027735728/en. June 3 EBITDA colour from https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/agilysys-ceo-sees-growth-phase-180513206.html. Both are company statements, so one source family.

findings.finding: The full-year subscription guide is back-end loaded, and Q2 is where a trim would show. Q1 FY27 subscription grew 26.1%, management steered Q2 to 'close to 30%', yet the FY guide was raised to '>=32%'. That requires roughly 35%+ subscription growth in Q3-Q4 (my arithmetic from ~$83.6M H1 against an FY26 base of ~$136M), on the Marriott PMS ramp and record backlog. The FY EBITDA guide (24%, Q4 'close to 30%') likewise needs H2 margin expansion. A reiteration is roughly neutral after the run-up; a trim or an implied H2 deceleration is the pattern that cost -20% in Jan 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Jan 2026: the FY subscription guide was reiterated at 29%, implying a Q4 deceleration to ~20%, and the stock fell -20% despite a revenue beat (https://www.itiger.com/news/1107151489). Oct 2025 and Jul 2026: guidance raises were bought +22.6% and +7.2%.
findings.why_not_priced: The arithmetic is public, so mostly priced. If the market doubted the H2 ramp, FY revenue consensus would sit well below the guide; it sits only just below, at $367.6M against a $368M low. The skew is balanced rather than put-bid, so the asymmetric downside is not visibly bought.
findings.independence: The company also says Marriott is excluded from backlog and backlog is at a record (Q1 call, same document family). The counter-evidence is that the guide was RAISED in July with Q2 already in view, which lowers the odds of a trim. That is why this is sized small.

findings.finding: US hotel demand was strong through the quarter. CoStar weekly RevPAR was +10.4% (week to 19 Sep) and +14.2% (week to 26 Sep, ADR record territory), after a 21-week growth streak broken only by the Labor Day shift, and Hilton guided Q3 system RevPAR to ~+4%. That is a supportive backdrop for hotel IT spend and property go-lives.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No evidence that this stock reacts to industry RevPAR. Agilysys revenue is driven by software deployments and backlog, not occupancy.
findings.why_not_priced: A public macro series. Transmission to Agilysys's quarter is unconfirmed by the company, which did not discuss macro on the Q1 call.
findings.independence: Proxy only. Hilton Q2 release Q3 outlook: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001585689/000158568926000042/q22026earningsrelease.htm. Weak Nevada fee collections (https://www.fox5vegas.com/2026/09/30/report-nevada-gaming-revenue-rises-314-august/) point the other way for the casino segment.

findings.finding: Customer-win press releases kept their cadence through the quarter and into October: Angel of the Winds chose the ecosystem (2026-09-22), 7 Cedars expanded (2026-09-29), casino resorts on the connected ecosystem (2026-10-20), and 40% of Golfweek's Top 100 resort courses use Agilysys Golf (2026-08-27). There is no sign of a sales slowdown after 'the best six-month sales period in company history'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Customer PRs have not moved the stock on their own. Bookings commentary on calls has fed the guide reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: Public PRs, mostly priced. The residual is the absence of a large chain win that would change the guide.
findings.independence: Q1 call: Q1 was the best April-June sales quarter on record, and the pipeline is larger than before (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/agys/transcripts/673731-q1-2027/). Company-sourced.

findings.finding: Q2 EPS estimate revisions ran 6 down and 1 up over the last 30 days while the $0.55 mean stayed flat (it was $0.57 90 days ago). The cuts are small, which nudges the EPS bar lower rather than higher into the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS was the line that decided the Jan 2026 -20% (adj EPS $0.42 vs $0.46).
findings.why_not_priced: Visible on every terminal. The residual is only that a lowered EPS bar on a margin-expansion year makes a miss less likely. The $0.55 also sits exactly on the 24% FY EBITDA cadence (Q2 ~22-23% margin on ~$91M), so a beat needs margin above the guide's implied path, which Q1 delivered.
